conventions.text:
Mention recount for the Coco Robotics Tranche 0 payload (conventions settled with the Coco session, Oct 19, 2026).

Two columns are reported for the three collision-prone names, side by side:
  strict      = the full name only: "Coco Robotics" (or "Coco's robots/delivery"), "Starship Technologies"
                (or "Starship robots/delivery"), "DoorDash Dot" / "DoorDash's Dot".
  contextual  = strict, plus a bare "Coco", "Starship" or "Dot" in the same sentence as a robot or
                delivery term (robot, robotics, delivery, sidewalk, bot, fleet, courier, autonomous,
                campus) or, for Dot, "DoorDash". Exclusions: Coco followed by Chanel/Gauff/Pixar/film/
                movie/nut; Starship preceded by SpaceX or followed by rocket/launch/Super Heavy.
                The merged payload's answers contain no SpaceX, Pixar or Chanel references.
Other companies: exact names (Serve Robotics, Kiwibot incl. "Kiwi bot", Avride, Nuro, Cartken, Ottonomy,
  White Rhino, Amazon Scout, Refraction AI, Tortoise and Figure AI in robot context); the list is open.
"DoorDash (app)" and "Uber Eats" are counted separately and are never Dot mentions.
People: "Zach Rash", or "Rash" in a sentence that also names Coco or Zach; "Brett Adcock", or "Adcock"
  in a sentence that also names Figure or Brett.
Proper nouns match case-sensitively (a lowercase hit is a URL fragment or a common word).
Unit: answers mentioning (an answer counts once however many times it names the entity); total_mentions
  is also given. answers_mentioning is computed on prose (answer text with URLs stripped);
  answers_link_only = the name appears only inside cited link URLs, never in the prose.
Halves reported separately with denominators; share of voice = unbranded answers only (150).
Per-question tables use the contextual forms.

usage: python3 recount_coco.py merged.json out.json
memo_rules: A company counts as named when its full name appears in an answer, or when its short name appears in a sentence about delivery robots (Coco, Starship, Dot).
A mention of DoorDash alone counts as the delivery app, not the Dot robot.
A person counts as named by full name, or by surname in a sentence about that person.
A topic counts when a sentence that names the company contains one of the topic's keywords.
A cited story centers on a company when its page names that company at least twice and at least twice as often as each of the other three.
PR share of voice = share of news and trade citations in unbranded answers going to stories centered on each company, each agent weighted equally.
Identical final URLs count once per answer; Gemini redirect links resolved to their publishers; dead links dropped and recorded.
